summary: Every student takes CLASSICS 220, CLASSICS 297 twice and CLASSICS 304, then the courses of one subplan: Ancient History, Classical Archaeology, or Language and Literature, each with its own language path. The audit checks those listed courses and the 135 graduate units. You check by hand the seminar and skills-course counts, the diagnostic, general and translation exams, the modern-language bibliography, the prospectus, teaching, candidacy, the oral exam and the dissertation.

XW0vLXsI.why: Option 2 was stored as a separate required rule beside "Ancient Language Coursework"; it moves inside that rule (MCU1W1eN) as the second option.

MCU1W1eN.why: "Ancient History Track students must take courses in both Latin and Greek, but can choose to focus more on one ancient language or emphasize broader linguistic skills by selecting a Single Language Emphasis (Option 1) or a Dual Language Emphasis (Option 2)". The data held only Option 1 here, with Option 2 required beside it. Special Topics courses in place of a Core quarter need the Director of Graduate Studies' pre-approval and are moved in by hand.

children.name: Option 1 - Single Language Emphasis
children.desc: Students focus more on one ancient language by taking 15 units of the core series (CLASSICS 201L/202L/203L or CLASSICS 201G/202G/203G) and five units of the alternate series, plus the Prose Composition or Syntax course/s in the primary ancient language selected

children.name: Option 2 - Dual Language Emphasis
children.desc: Students emphasize broader linguistic skills. This requires students to take both ancient language series.
